name: Arethusa
domains: evening nymph of the western garden

summary.text: The fourth Hesperid in Apollodorus' named roll beside Ladon — Aegle, Erythia, Hesperia, and Arethusa — not to be confused with the Sicilian spring of that name pursued by Alpheus (Ovid, Pausanias) or with Homer's spring on Ithaca.

story.text: Apollodorus alone among our seven lenses names an Arethusa among the apple-guardians at Atlas' garden. With Ladon and her three sisters she kept the golden fruit that Earth gave Hera — the same western watch where Heracles came for his eleventh labour.

Several figures bear the name: Ovid's Arethusa fled Alpheus from Elis to Ortygia and witnessed Proserpina's rape; Homer knows a spring Arethusa on Ithaca; Hyginus lists other Arethusas among Nereids and in unrelated genealogies. Apollodorus' western evening sister is not the Sicilian spring.

Apollonius' Argonautica episode at the garden names only Aegle, Erytheis, and Hespere after Ladon's death; Arethusa is absent from that three-name roll but remains in Apollodorus' quartet. The parentage of the Hesperides as a whole remains disputed.
